Consult Summary:
- 23-year-old female with worsening constant lower abdominal pain over several days, associated with light vaginal bleeding and recent constipation.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Lower abdominal pain, constant, midline below the belly button, started a few days ago, worsening, pain rated 8/10.
- Associated symptoms: Nausea without vomiting, light pink vaginal bleeding, recent constipation (resolved), small amount of vaginal discharge.
- Pertinent negatives: No fever, no faintness, no abnormal urinary symptoms, no difficulty breathing, no shoulder pain, no diarrhea, no blood in stool or urine, maintaining normal activities.
- Last menstrual period: 2–3 weeks ago; prior periods irregular but occurring, last period reported as normal.
- Sexual history: Regular intercourse, last intercourse 4 days ago; uses contraceptive implant (Implanon) for past year.
- Pregnancy test: Last done one month ago (prior to onset of abdominal pain); no pregnancy or prior pregnancies.
- Past medical history: Allergy to amoxicillin.
- Medications: Contraceptive implant (Implanon); dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Surgery: No prior surgeries.
- Social history: School teacher; lives with husband and husband's family; does not use recreational drugs; alcohol and smoking status unclear ("I don't know"); returned from abroad over a year ago.

Examination:
- (No examination findings documented.)
- (No documented vitals.)

Impression:
- Worsening lower abdominal pain in reproductive-aged female, with light vaginal bleeding and recent constipation. Differential to include gynecological causes (e.g., early pregnancy complications, pelvic infection), among others.

Plan:
- Arrange face-to-face examination and abdominal assessment in clinic.
- Advise patient to repeat pregnancy test today; if positive, contact provider urgently.
- Instructed to arrange appointment via support line.
- Advised to seek urgent care if unable to tolerate fluids or if symptoms worsen prior to appointment.

Quality checks:

●	Missing clinically expected elements: medication reconciliation and full list, confirmation of other allergies, detailed menstrual history, family history, comprehensive review of systems, documented vitals or examination findings, alcohol and smoking status (“I don’t know” given as answer).
●	No internal conflicts identified.
●	Transcript quality: Some audio ambiguities, minor missing data, but clinically relevant information mostly captured. Social and preventive history partially incomplete.
